claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch based on aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and rollout controls, despite an exposed below-target aviation maintenance triage use case and no completed approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if the material limitation for the named launch use case was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Operational readiness evidence can support launch confidence, but it does not satisfy the separate disclosure/approval predicate in the policy.
If the affected segment remains exposed and neither disclosure nor approved risk acceptance is in evidence, certification is not compliant on this record.
evidence_requests: Provide the final model-card or equivalent launch disclosure showing the aviation maintenance triage limitation was explicitly disclosed before launch.
Provide an approved risk acceptance signed by the authorized approver that explicitly addresses aviation maintenance triage exposure.
Provide evidence that the affected aviation maintenance triage segment was excluded from the initial rollout cohort, if that changed.
Provide any updated evaluation showing the below-target deferred-defect routing issue was resolved before certification.
specific_concerns: The affected aviation maintenance triage segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The segment is below target on deferred-defect routing, indicating a live material limitation for a named launch use case.
The risk acceptance record is not approved: the approver line is blank.
The draft risk acceptance does not mention the aviation maintenance triage exposure.
The policy requires disclosure of material limitations unless they are resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The governing policy text explicitly says rollout controls do not cure the weakness when the affected segment remains exposed.
unsupported_claims: That rollout controls and monitoring are sufficient to support certification while the exposed named use case remains in scope.
That a 6% gate, rollback switch, or public risk-management principles can substitute for the required disclosure or approved risk acceptance predicate.
That certification is compliant on the present record, rather than merely operationally understandable.
